opening: Can you tell me where you were on the night of {date}?
How do you know the victim?
When was the last time you saw the victim?
Can anyone verify your whereabouts during the time in question?
What is your relationship to the victim?
alibi: What were you doing between {time1} and {time2}?
Can you provide any documentation of your whereabouts?
Why should I believe your alibi?
motive: Did you have any disputes with the victim?
Do you have any reason to harm the victim?
Were you aware of the victim's activities?
Did you benefit from this crime?
What were your feelings toward the victim?
opportunity: How well do you know the area where the crime occurred?
Do you own or have access to {item}?
Were you familiar with the victim's routine?
confrontational: We have evidence that contradicts your statement.
Your story doesn't add up. Want to tell me the truth?
We know you were there. Why lie about it?
This will go easier if you cooperate.
Do you understand the seriousness of this situation?
empathetic: I understand this must be difficult for you.
Help me understand what happened from your perspective.
Is there anything you want to tell me?
I can see you're troubled by this. Let's talk about it.
Sometimes accidents happen. Is that what occurred here?

cooperative_innocent: I was at home with my family that night.
I want to help with your investigation.
I understand. Ask me anything you need to know.
cooperative_guilty: I... I might have been near there.
I didn't mean for things to go that far.
There's something I should tell you.
uncooperative_innocent: I don't have to answer that.
I've told you everything I know.
uncooperative_guilty: I don't know what you're talking about.
nervous: Can I have a moment to think?
defensive: You should be looking for the real criminal!

empathetic.description: Build rapport and trust with the subject

tactical.description: Use strategic questioning and evidence presentation
